entries.title: Loch Modan
body: A temperate land in eastern Khaz Modan, where grey, rugged mountains rise on every side around a great lake, and the hills are lightly wooded with pine and birch. The Loch is the largest body of water in Khaz Modan, held in place by the Stonewrought Dam, an architectural wonder without equal in Azeroth.

For all its calm, the loch has seen its share of bloodshed. Today its dangers come from below: troggs, dug up from the deep places by the dwarves' own excavations, have spread through the mountains and built crude camps from which they fall on travellers. Kobolds, ogres and Dark Iron saboteurs complete the list.

entries.title: Thelsamar
body: The dwarven town on the western shore of the loch, north of Grizzlepaw Ridge, with a gryphon roost, a forge and an inn. The road to the passes into Dun Morogh and the Wetlands runs just west of it, and travellers bound for the Badlands and Uldaman come through on their way south.
Thelsamar is also known for its blood sausages, which its cook makes from whatever the hills provide.

entries.title: Stoutlager Inn
body: The inn of Thelsamar and one of the most popular places in Loch Modan, a warm stopping point for anyone crossing the mountains, with drink and company enough for a long evening.

entries.title: Dun Algaz
body: The tunnelled pass between Loch Modan and the Wetlands, and the stronghold that guards it. It is older than the War of the Three Hammers; the Wildhammer clan went north through it when they were driven out of Ironforge.

In the Second War, the orcs fell back here after their defeat at Dun Modr. Anduin Lothar ordered the outpost destroyed and failed, and it became the Horde's last hold in Khaz Modan. Years later, Nekros Skullcrusher moved his Dragonmaw clan into caves hidden in the pass. The mountaineers of Algaz Station still keep watch on the Loch Modan side.

entries.title: The Northern Guard Tower
body: The guard post on the North Gate Pass, where the road climbs west into Dun Morogh. It is the pass most travellers take to and from the Wetlands, and Mountaineer Stormpike's men watch it from Algaz Station.

entries.title: The Valley of Kings
body: A green valley in the south-western corner of Loch Modan, on the road from the South Gate Pass. Its gate to the Searing Gorge is kept locked and guarded.

Over the valley stand two great statues of the dwarven kings Madoran Bronzebeard and Khardros Wildhammer, commissioned by their sons after their deaths. They guard the pass into the south, which had turned volcanic under Ragnaros' scorching presence, as a warning to any who would attack the dwarven kingdoms, and as a reminder of the price the Dark Irons paid for their crimes.

entries.title: Stonesplinter Valley
body: A valley among the mountains of south-western Loch Modan, once pristine and now crawling with troggs of the Stonesplinter tribe. Their leader, Grawmug, keeps to the heart of the valley, and the dwarves would dearly like to see him gone.

entries.title: Silver Stream Mine
body: A mine in the north of Loch Modan that was once a bountiful source of silver for Ironforge. It was worked out long ago, and the Miners' League turned it into a storage depot. Its walls still yield the charged rift gems mages use in their robes.
Tunnel Rat kobolds have taken the whole mine for themselves.

entries.title: Stonewrought Dam
body: The massive dam along Loch Modan's northern edge, one of the most impressive wonders of the world. It more than doubles the size of the loch, and its waters run on into the flooded plains of the Wetlands.

Few know it is the work of a Dark Iron: the great architect Franclorn Forgewright oversaw its building and invented the stonewrought method it is named for. Now the Dark Iron clan attacks it, and Ironforge has had to tighten its guard. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII oversees it.

entries.title: The Loch
body: The great lake itself, the largest body of water in Khaz Modan and the third largest in the known world after Lordamere and Darrowmere. Its islands and its bottom are strewn with broken catapults and ballistae from the Second War, mute evidence of the region's bloody history. Crocolisks hunt in the shallows.

entries.title: Mo'grosh Stronghold
body: A set of ogre-infested caves in north-eastern Loch Modan, home of the Mo'grosh ogres. Under their leader Chok'sul they have coordinated attacks against Thelsamar, the Stonewrought Dam and the dwarves' excavation sites.
One of their bands ambushed a dwarven ore caravan coming from the Wetlands and left only a single dying guard alive.

entries.title: Ironband's Excavation Site
body: An extensive dwarven dig in south-eastern Loch Modan. Like the Explorers' League's other sites, in the Wetlands, Darkshore, the Badlands and at Uldaman, it has been overrun by hostile creatures that drove off the prospectors and miners. Here the culprits are troggs of a particularly large and volatile breed.
The irony is not lost on the dwarves: it was their own digging that woke the troggs in the first place.

entries.title: The Farstrider Lodge
body: A hunters' lodge in south-eastern Loch Modan, built in the high elven style by the Farstriders, the rangers of Quel'Thalas. Only one high elf still lives there; its other residents are human and dwarven hunters who came for the loch's game.

entries.title: Grizzlepaw Ridge
body: The mountains south of Thelsamar, home to a large pack of bears. The most ferocious of them, Ol' Sooty, sometimes wanders down from his lair into the valley and falls on anyone unlucky enough to irritate him.

entries.title: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII
body: The engineer in charge of the Stonewrought Dam, the seventh of his line. Since the Dark Iron attacks began, he has made it his business to rid Loch Modan of the saboteurs before they can bring the dam down.

entries.title: Grawmug
body: The leader of the Stonesplinter troggs. He holds the heart of Stonesplinter Valley, and claims the loch for his tribe.

entries.title: Chok'sul
body: The leader of the Mo'grosh ogres. It is Chok'sul who coordinates their raids on Thelsamar, the dam and the excavation sites.

entries.title: Prospector Ironband
body: An unlucky prospector of the Explorers' League whose excavation in Loch Modan was overrun by troggs. He has not given up: he recruits help to clear his site, and keeps watch on the League's other digs, all the way down to Uldaman.

entries.title: The Second War in Khaz Modan
body: In the Second War the Horde overran Khaz Modan. The orcs took Loch Modan and made their stand there against the Alliance, and the dwarves of Ironforge held out in their mountain until the tide turned.
When the war ended the dwarves reclaimed the loch. The wrecked catapults and ballistae lying on its bottom and its islands are all that is left of the orcish occupation.

entries.title: The Dark Iron Plot
body: The Dark Iron dwarves have never forgiven the Bronzebeards and Wildhammers for the War of the Three Hammers, nor forgotten the price they paid when Thaurissan's summoning loosed Ragnaros on the south.
Their saboteurs now creep into the dwarven lands, and their latest target is the Stonewrought Dam, which one of their own built. If it broke, the loch would pour out into the Wetlands.
sources: page text 1914 (War of the Three Hammers)

entries.title: The Trogg Plague
body: Troggs are a primitive race that lived deep beneath the earth, near the titans' ancient works. The dwarves' excavations in search of their own origins broke into their caves, and the troggs came up.
They have since settled the mountains of Khaz Modan in crude camps and caves. Every dig of the Explorers' League seems to end the same way, overrun by the creatures it uncovered.
